rigid-body.def: An object or system that keeps its shape as it moves, so every part of it turns through the same angle in the same time.

axis-of-rotation.def: The line about which an object turns. Every point of the object moves in a circle centered on this line.

radian.def: The SI unit of angle: the angle for which the distance along a circle equals the radius. One revolution is 2π rad, about 6.28 rad, or 360°.

angular-displacement.def: The change in an object’s angle, Δθ = θ − θ₀, in radians, with a sign for the direction of turning (counterclockwise positive is a common choice).

angular-velocity.def: The rate of change of angle, ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad/s. Its sign says whether the object turns clockwise or counterclockwise.

angular-acceleration.def: The rate of change of angular velocity, α = Δω/Δt, in rad/s². When α and ω have the same sign the object speeds up; opposite signs, it slows.

rotational-kinematic-equations.def: For constant angular acceleration: ω = ω₀ + αt, θ = θ₀ + ω₀t + ½αt², and ω² = ω₀² + 2α(θ − θ₀). They mirror the linear equations with θ, ω, α for x, v, a.
